title: How to Get Multiple Architect Proposals for Your Westchester Project
excerpt: Getting more than one proposal helps you make the right choice for your home. Here's what to know about working with architects in Westchester County.
content:
When you're planning a renovation, addition, or new construction project, it makes sense to talk to more than one professional. A licensed architect in Westchester, NY can help you understand what's possible, what it will take to get permits, and what the actual work will involve. But how do you find them, and what should you ask for when you reach out?

The truth is that most homeowners don't shop around enough. They talk to one contractor, get one idea, and move forward. That's a missed opportunity. Getting multiple proposals gives you a real picture of your options and helps you feel confident in your decision.

Start by Being Clear About Your Project

Before you call anyone, write down what you want. Are you adding a second story to your home in Scarsdale? Renovating your kitchen in Mamaroneck? Converting an open concept in Rye? The clearer you are about your goals, the better proposals you'll get back.

Put it all in one document. Include photos of your home. Describe what's not working now. List the must-haves and the nice-to-haves. This document becomes your request for proposal, and it helps every architect or contractor understand your project the same way.

Don't worry about being too detailed. Architects and contractors want to know what you're thinking. It saves everyone time and makes sure the proposals are actually comparable.

Know What to Look for in a Design-Build Firm

When you're looking for professionals to work with, there's an important distinction. Some firms separate their design work from their construction work. A design-build approach in Westchester means one firm handles both the architecture and the building, which can be simpler for homeowners.

A general contractor in Westchester needs to know how to build things. A licensed architect in New York needs to know how to design them legally and safely. When one person is both, like Silvio M. Luca, who runs House Architecture & Construction, PLLC, you have clear accountability. He's licensed as both an architect and a general contractor in New York State, and he oversees every project personally.

This matters whether you're in Bronxville, Harrison, or Ossining. Each town has its own building department and permit requirements. Having one professional who understands both the design and the permitting process can save you headaches.

What to Ask for in Each Proposal

When you reach out to firms, ask for a written proposal. This should include a scope of work, a timeline, and how they plan to manage the project. Ask how they handle permits in your specific town. Ask about their experience with projects like yours.

If you want home additions in Westchester or a custom home in Westchester County, ask to see photos of similar work. Ask for references. Call those references. This isn't just about price, it's about whether you can work with this person for months while they're in your home.

Get at least two or three proposals. You'll start to see patterns. One contractor might suggest a different approach than another. One might have a longer timeline. These differences matter, and they help you make a real choice instead of just picking a name.
